docs.title: Article — Brookfield Business News
docs.text: BROOKFIELD (March 3) — Tech company Novaline announced yesterday that it will move its headquarters from Chicago to Brookfield by the end of the year. The company, which makes software for hospitals, currently employs 300 people. It plans to hire 150 more in Brookfield over the next two years. [1] Novaline chose Brookfield because of its lower office costs and its close connection to Brookfield University, which has a strong computer science program. [2] The new headquarters will be in the renovated Carlton Building on River Street. [3] Mayor Ellen Sato welcomed the news, saying it would bring "high-quality jobs" to the city. [4]

qs.q: What is the article mainly about?
qs.why: will move its headquarters from Chicago to Brookfield.

qs.why: makes software for hospitals.

qs.why: Sau câu nói về trường đại học (nguồn sinh viên mới tốt nghiệp) và trước câu về toà nhà.
